The US Food and Drug Administration has recalled breakfast sandwiches over fears they’re contaminated with a terrifying organism linked to fatal infections, stillbirths, and miscarriages.

Grand Strand Sandwich Company Inc. asked to rip the items from shelves on Thursday after discovering the dangerous contaminant.

Its Lunch Box-branded sandwiches, which were sold in North Carolina, South Carolina, and Virginia, potentially contain Listeria monocytogenes, an organism which can cause the serious infection listeriosis, the FDA announced.

The affected products were distributed between March 2 and Nov. 10 and include:

The sandwiches were sold at convenience stores, vending machines and prison canteens. No illnesses have been linked to the items.

Those with weaker immune systems who contract the bug like young children, elderly people, and pregnant women could face short-term symptoms like high fever, severe headaches, nausea, diarrhea, abdominal pain and diarrhea.

Pregnant women could also suffer miscarriages, stillbirths, premature delivery or life-threatening infection of the newborn if the nasty organism infects the fetus.

Anyone who has purchased a recalled item is urged to throw the item away immediately, especially if it could be hiding in the back of a freezer or pantry.

Affected products can be redeemed for a refund if the packaging is brought to the retailer where it was bought.

Shoppers with questions about the recall can contact Grand Strand Sandwich at 843-399-2999 from Monday to Thursday between the hours of 8 p.m. and 4 p.m. and on Friday between 8 a.m. and 12 p.m.

This latest recall came just days after 2,414 other breakfast sandwiches were also recalled over listeria fears.

در نتایج جستجوی خود، پوشش خبری بیشتر ما را مشاهده کنید. اداره غذا و داروی ایالات متحده به دلیل نگرانی از آلودگی ساندویچ‌های صبحانه به یک ارگانیسم وحشتناک که با عفونت‌های کشنده، تولد نوزاد مرده و سقط جنین مرتبط است، این محصولات را فراخوان کرد. شرکت Grand Strand Sandwich Inc. روز پنجشنبه پس از کشف این آلاینده خطرناک، خواستار جمع‌آوری این محصولات از قفسه‌ها شد. سازمان غذا و داروی آمریکا اعلام کرد که ساندویچ‌های این شرکت با برند Lunch Box که در کارولینای شمالی، کارولینای جنوبی و ویرجینیا فروخته می‌شدند، احتمالاً حاوی لیستریا مونوسیتوژنز هستند؛ موجودی که می‌تواند باعث عفونت جدی لیستریاز شود. محصولات آلوده بین 2 مارس تا 10 نوامبر توزیع شده‌اند و شامل موارد زیر هستند:
این ساندویچ‌ها در فروشگاه‌های شبانه‌روزی، دستگاه‌های فروش خودکار و بوفه‌های زندان فروخته می‌شدند. هیچ بیماری‌ای به این محصولات مرتبط نشده است. افرادی که سیستم ایمنی ضعیف‌تری دارند و به این میکروب مبتلا می‌شوند، مانند کودکان خردسال، افراد مسن و زنان باردار، ممکن است با علائمی کوتاه‌مدت مانند تب بالا، سردردهای شدید، حالت تهوع، اسهال، درد شکم و اسهال مواجه شوند. همچنین اگر این موجود ناخوشایند جنین را آلوده کند، زنان باردار ممکن است دچار سقط جنین، تولد نوزاد مرده، زایمان زودرس یا عفونت تهدیدکننده حیات نوزاد شوند. از هر کسی که محصول فراخوان شده‌ای را خریداری کرده است، اکیداً خواسته می‌شود که فوراً آن محصول را دور بیندازد، به‌ویژه اگر ممکن است در قسمت پشتی فریزر یا انباری پنهان شده باشد. در صورت بردن بسته‌بندی محصولات آسیب‌دیده به فروشگاهی که از آن خریداری شده‌اند، می‌توان وجه آنها را پس گرفت. خریدارانی که در مورد فراخوان سؤال دارند، می‌توانند با شماره تلفن 1-800-CDC-INFO تماس بگیرند.

A Florida woman claims she was bullied out of the waterfront condo she inherited from her late mother amid a bitter $323 million developer buyout — with a broker allegedly calling her a “psychotic witch” and a “nutcase” in a campaign to pressure her into selling.

Melanie Seymour Holland, a unit owner at Portofino South in West Palm Beach, has sued developer BEKO Equities and real estate broker Greg Greer, accusing them of an “extraordinary pressure campaign” that turned her longtime sanctuary into a place of fear, the Real Deal reported.

The dispute centers on the 140-unit waterfront building at 3800 Washington Road, which overlooks President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago estate across the Intracoastal Waterway. BEKO, a joint venture involving O.D. Kobo and Gilbert Benhamou’s Immocorp, is attempting to acquire every apartment for a whopping $323.4 million sum.

The developer has secured agreements from 108 owners, but the deal requires unanimous approval to terminate the condo association.

Holland, a vocal critic of rapid development, claims she became a particular target after resisting the buyout.

According to the lawsuit, Greer sent emails to more than 100 residents, board members and attorneys accusing her of making “extortionate demands” on behalf of 26 owners.

He allegedly branded her a “psychotic witch,” a “nutcase” and a “self-centered narcissist,” while encouraging neighbors to confront her.

The alleged intimidation even reached her doorstep.

When Holland returned to her apartment in early November, she discovered a small broom, a nursing home brochure and a note reading, “They have a dementia unit that’s perfect for the two of you,” according to the complaint.

“For Mrs. Holland, paradise is now a place of fear,” the lawsuit states. “Because of this targeted campaign, the apartment her mother left her as a sanctuary is now a place she is afraid to enter.”

Her attorney, William A. Brewer III, said she had been “targeted, vilified and ostracized.”

BEKO has strongly denied the allegations.

Lee Goldstein, the developer’s head of legal affairs, called the claims “entirely without merit,” insisting Greer was never employed or compensated by BEKO and that the company neither directed nor knew about his alleged conduct.

The developer has since severed ties with the broker.

In a Nov. 12 letter to residents, Kobo said his team would take over negotiations directly and assured owners that no one would be forced to sell.

BEKO has also offered an additional $200,000 per unit to owners who sign agreements by Jan. 8.

The proposed deal values apartments at roughly $1,800 to $2,000 per square foot — nearly three times their estimated market value, according to the developer.

But the financial pressure extends beyond the buyout.

Built in 1971, Portofino South faces more than $10 million in assessments, highlighting the mounting costs confronting aging Florida condo buildings.

As The Post previously reported, soaring HOA fees, special assessments and insurance costs are leaving some condo owners struggling to sell their homes.

The fight has also taken an uglier turn, with BEKO raising concerns about AI-generated imagery depicting Holland holding a platter bearing the severed head of one of its managing partners.

The developer said it believes law enforcement should review the material.
news.content: در نتایج جستجوی خود، پوشش خبری بیشتر ما را ببینید. یک زن اهل فلوریدا ادعا می‌کند که در جریان یک معامله خرید 323 میلیون دلاری توسط سازنده، از آپارتمان ساحلی که از مادر مرحومش به ارث برده بود، با زور بیرون رانده شده است — ظاهراً یک دلال در کمپینی برای تحت فشار قرار دادن او برای فروش، او را «جادوگر روانی» و «دیوانه» خطاب کرده است. طبق گزارش Real Deal، ملانی سیمور هالند، مالک یک واحد در پورتوفینو ساوت در وست پالم بیچ، از شرکت سازنده BEKO Equities و دلال املاک و مستغلات گرگ گریر شکایت کرده و آنها را به «کمپین فشار فوق‌العاده‌ای» متهم کرده است که پناهگاه دیرینه‌اش را به مکانی پر از ترس تبدیل کرده است. این اختلاف بر سر ساختمان 140 واحدی ساحلی در جاده واشنگتن 3800 است که مشرف به ملک مار-آ-لاگو رئیس جمهور دونالد ترامپ در سراسر آبراه درون ساحلی است. BEKO، یک سرمایه گذاری مشترک شامل O.D. Immocorp متعلق به کوبو و گیلبرت بنهامو در تلاش است تا هر آپارتمان را با مبلغ هنگفت 323.4 میلیون دلار خریداری کند. توسعه‌دهنده موافقت‌نامه‌هایی را از 108 مالک تضمین کرده است، اما این معامله برای خاتمه دادن به کاندو نیاز به تأیید اتفاق آرا دارد. هلند، منتقد سرسخت توسعه سریع، ادعا می‌کند که پس از مقاومت در برابر خرید، به یک هدف خاص تبدیل شده است. طبق این شکایت، گریر به بیش از 100 نفر از ساکنان، اعضای هیئت مدیره و وکلای خود ایمیل‌هایی ارسال کرد. صاحبان او ظاهراً او را "جادوگر روان پریشی"، "دورگیر" و "خودمحور" نامید، در حالی که همسایگان را تشویق به مقابله با او کرد.

A hauntingly beautiful image of the ‘Tribute in Light’ 9/11 memorial has earned a coveted spot on National Geographic’s Pictures of the Year list — in what its photographer called an ode to the Big Apple.

Christopher Payne’s photo, called “Beam of Hope,” captures the moment electricians and artists gazed up at the high-powered spotlights that make up the famous ghostly image of the Twin Towers in the New York skyline, after they spent more than a week assembling them for the annual display.

The shot is so close to the powerful display that the viewer can differentiate the tiny streams of light that together make up the dual beams — with the staging set up so that there are dozens of smaller Twin Towers standing together.

“It’s almost like a rainbow of hope going up into the sky, but most people don’t know where it starts from. So I always thought of that picture of being inside the array of 88 lights. It’s like being in the pot of gold. You found where the rainbow starts,” Payne told The Post Friday.

“I knew it was going to be the money shot. It expressed everything: a sense of wonder, but also a sense of how they do it and that ‘aha’ moment.”

The stunning image was plucked from millions of submissions from around the globe for the spot on the 25 picture list — marking Payne’s second time in three years receiving the honor.

“Beam of Hope” is also just one of two taken in the US, the second of which, by Brent Stirton, captures two girls playing among compost mounds on their family’s Washington farm.

Payne snapped the breathtaking image ahead of the 25th anniversary of the terror attacks as he watched crews tediously erect the annual sculpture.

It took crews nine days to install the 88 individual 7,000-watt xenon compressed gas lightbulbs, which give the illusion of two massive rays of light beaming into the sky.

“From anywhere else, it seems so magical and then you get there and you realize that it’s just a bunch of these massive lights arranged in a very particular way, very intentional,” explained Payne, calling the experience “grounding.”

Payne took a variety of photographs for the project, including one of children and family members of 9/11 victims running beneath the beam’s glow.

But it was the image of the crews admiring their work that landed a spot on the coveted list.

“For them it’s a reunion. They do it not for the money, not because they’re learning anything new, but they do this because they feel it’s important and significant, and it gives them a chance to reconnect. That’s something that I didn’t anticipate,” said Payne, adding that every worker had a connection to the terror attacks.

“It’s very much about New York City.”
news.content:
بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. تصویری بسیار زیبا از یادبود «تقدیر در نور» 11 سپتامبر، جایگاه مورد علاقه‌ای را در فهرست تصاویر سال نشنال جئوگرافیک به دست آورده است - چیزی که عکاسش آن را قصیده‌ای برای سیب بزرگ نامیده است. عکس کریستوفر پین که «پرتو امید» نام دارد، لحظه‌ای را به تصویر می‌کشد که برق‌کارها و هنرمندان به نورافکن‌های پرقدرتی که تصویر شبح‌آلود معروف برج‌های دوقلو در افق نیویورک را تشکیل می‌دهند، خیره می‌شوند، پس از اینکه بیش از یک هفته وقت صرف جمع‌آوری آن‌ها برای نمایش سالانه کردند. شات آنقدر به نمایشگر قدرتمند نزدیک است که بیننده می‌تواند جریان‌های کوچک نور را که با هم پرتوهای دوگانه را تشکیل می‌دهند، متمایز کند - با صحنه‌سازی به‌گونه‌ای که ده‌ها برج دوقلوی کوچک‌تر کنار هم ایستاده‌اند. «تقریباً شبیه یک رنگین کمان امید است که به آسمان می‌رود، اما بیشتر مردم نمی‌دانند که نور از کجا شروع می‌شود. مثل قرار گرفتن در ظرف طلاست. پین به The Post Friday گفت: «تو متوجه شدی که رنگین کمان از کجا شروع می شود. همه چیز را بیان می کرد: یک حس شگفتی، اما همچنین یک حس از نحوه انجام آن و آن لحظه "آها".

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

There are four very healthy signs for the future of Nocturne in this week’s episode on Apple TV. One of those signs wears bikini briefs.

The episode begins three years ago, as Jonah confronts a still-free Jurek Walter, his primary suspect in the murders they’ve been uncovering. When Jurek snorts out a booger while taunting the cop, Jonah pockets the thing. As we know, he eventually plants it to ensure Walter’s conviction, a conspiracy his partner and chief were both in on as well.

Back in the present, a hunter stumbles across one of Jurek Walter’s trademark burial sites, complete with air pipe, and Jonah — now fired from the task force by Quinn and acting on his own — shows up to investigate. Upsettingly, the living grave contains the skeletal remains of two dogs who clearly suffered before they died, as did Walter’s human victims. Using their literal dog tags, Jonah shows up at the home of their owner. Instead, he’s greeted by a furious man wearing green underwear.

“I’m not in any rush, if you wanna go put your pants on,” Jonah says awkwardly.

We have a joke, ladies and gentlemen! Nocturne told a joke! I didn’t think any of these sad sacks had it in ’em.

The underwear guy (Ben Chase) winds up being surprisingly (suspiciously?) open when he learns the nature of Jonah’s visit. Turns out the dogs belonged to his Uncle Pat, who loved them deeply, but who died from a fall down some slippery stairs a couple years earlier. Couple this untimely demise with the security camera on the garage and the man’s general state of, y’know, pantslessness, and Jonah naturally suspects he’s stumbled across Jurek’s accomplice.

If you’ve ever watched Breaking Bad or the first season of True Detective, however, you know that a criminal walking around in his underwear isn’t a sign of murder holes, but meth labs. Sure enough, that’s what Jonah and his unwitting partner Chief Dave (who shows up to the place looking for him later that night) discover after they have a physical fight with both underwear man and his hulking accomplice (Matthew Willig). This, too, is some funny stuff. Bill Camp kissing some tweaker upside the cranium with an aluminum baseball bat like a Primus song? Gimme all o’ that ya got!

The two sides wind up reaching something of a legal Mexican standoff. These two guys run an underground meth lab — that’s the reason for the countless air pipes sticking out of their backyard soil, thank god — and have just been beaten up and tied up, so they’re theoretically in deep trouble. However, they quickly note that no one has produced a warrant, and we at home know Jonah isn’t even a real cop anymore, so theoretically it’s he and Dave who are in deep trouble.

In what strikes me as gentlemanly arrangement, Jonah and Dave agree to call the whole thing off in exchange for the truth about Uncle Pat. Turns out he didn’t fall down the stairs, but nor was he murdered, not by these guys and not by Jurek’s accomplice. He hanged himself in despair after losing those dogs, whom he loved like children.

Here’s where good sign for the future number two pops up. Driving home, Dave mentions his AA sponsor, which gets the two men to thinking. Two people from the meetings Dave attended disappeared; a third, whom they sponsored, drank himself to death not long after. You don’t suppose…?

“Maybe the victims aren’t the victims,” Jonah says.

And just like that, we have some insight into why Jurek’s victims appear to be of all genders and ages, a relative rarity for serial killers. He wasn’t targeting them at all, he was targeting people who’d be driven to suicide by their disappearances and deaths — up to and including Jonah’s partner and Saga’s father Sam Mendel, who shot himself after his wife Rebecca vanished. The victims had no pattern, because they were looking at the wrong people.

Sure enough, poor Michael Frost, the surviving victim, reveals the next piece of the puzzle. Afraid to go outside, traumatized by a visit to a diner, he sits in his closet trying to convince his mother IDA to play hangman over a three-letter word. “MOM” isn’t right, but he tells her she’s “so close.”

The answer, of course, is “IDA,” and the Sandman, who forced him to play this game with her, wants her to kill herself. Only then will her daughter be returned safely.

Well, this is certainly innovative in the serial-killing space! That there have never been Arkham Asylum level campaigns of four-dimensional murder chess like the one Jurek Walter and his accomplice are playing with the authorities is obvious. But there have been plenty in the movies and on TV. None that I know of were selecting their victims in hopes of provoking a second wave of deaths — one that apparently his accomplice is helping along.

We must go back inside Riverdale Psychiatric Hospital for the final two reasons to be psyched for the remainder of the series. First, Saga Bauer, aka Esther Desjardins, has begun matching wits with Walter by communicating with him through their toilet pipes. (A symbolism-rich choice, to be sure.) Though neither Jonah nor Agent Quinn had any idea she’d gotten herself that close, their colleague Nate encourages them to leave her where she is, as it’s their best hope of getting info out of Walter. Sure enough, he reveals a location he says is important to him, though of course it could be another wild goose chase.

The point here, though, is that this means Stephen Graham and Zazie Beetz are now going to do a bunch of acting together. That’s something I’ve been looking forward to since it was first introduced as a possibility.

Just look at the dividends it’s paying with Graham and Rory Culkin, who plays his nurse Karl — point four in our promising signs for the future. Instead of beating around the bush, Nate and Quinn immediately detain Karl for delivering messages for Walter, a federal offense. But he can stay out of prison by passing them information about anything unusual going on. Meanwhile, he maintains his relationship with Walter, passing him information about his new roommate “Esther.” He even admits the cops are onto him, that they want information, and that they’re talking about having Esther moved to avoid distractions.

But Karl doesn’t know that Esther’s an undercover agent, so he’s saying all this stuff within her earshot. Meanwhile, Jurek begins talking to Esther, even though he’s so suspicious she’s a cop he comes out and asks her right away. Nocturne is choosing to move things along rather than drag them out. Yes, they catch Karl. Yes, he tells Jurek. Yes, Saga hears it all.

Humor, innovation, and a willingness to sh-t or get off the pot: These qualities can’t help but help Nocturne moving forward, however many holes they stumble into on the way.

Sean T. Collins (@seantcollins.com on Bluesky and theseantcollins on Patreon) has written about television for The New York Times, Vulture, Rolling Stone, and elsewhere. He is the author of Pain Don’t Hurt: Meditations on Road House. He lives with his family on Long Island.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Luna Moore thought she was doing the responsible thing by taking an Uber.

She and her best friend, Emily Normandin-Parker, had been enjoying the last weeks of summer in August 2023, drinking at a bar in Southern California, and neither intended to get behind the wheel.

But while traveling home along the freeway, Moore became nauseous — in part, she said, because their Uber driver, a man named Vu Tran, was repeatedly swerving between lanes.

Unable to find a bag, Moore rolled down the window and vomited.

Rather than finding a safe place to pull over, Tran stopped on a triangular stretch of pavement separating the freeway from an exit ramp, ordered the women out of his vehicle, and demanded a $300 cleaning fee, Moore recalled.

Stranded along the dark highway, Normandin-Parker began walking away in search of help. Moore said she tried to follow her friend, but Tran blocked her path.

“He stood directly between me and Emily, and he was screaming in my face,” Moore told The Post.

Fearing their confrontation could turn physical, Moore frantically took down Tran’s payment information, hoping to appease him long enough to go after her friend.

By then, Normandin-Parker had made her way into traffic, where she was struck and killed by another vehicle. She was 23.

In the nearly three years that followed, Moore not only had to grapple with the loss of her best friend but was made to revisit some of the darkest moments of her own life.

Normandin-Parker’s parents pursued wrongful-death claims against Uber and Tran, while Moore brought her own claims for damages. The claims were handled together, with Moore also serving as a witness in the parents’ case.

But it’s the inappropriately invasive way Moore was questioned during the legal battle that she takes most issue with.

She told The Post she faced detailed questions from defense attorneys not just about the alcohol she had drunk that night, but inappropriate questions about her childhood medical history, what she was wearing that night and her experience of sexual abuse when she was 16.

“I constantly feel it should have been me who died instead of Emily,”  Moore, now 27, told The Post.

Uber denied questioning Moore during the arbitration hearing and told The Post that lawyers independently retained by Tran were responsible for the invasive questioning.

However, a deposition transcript reviewed by The Post shows that Uber’s attorneys questioned Moore about her mental health and how she paid for her medication, revisiting some topics previously raised by the driver’s counsel.

And attorneys who have battled Uber say Moore’s experience is not an isolated complaint.

Lawyers told The Post that passengers seeking compensation for physical injuries sustained in ordinary car crashes and those involved in wrongful-death litigation have also faced sweeping demands for medical records, questions about childhood trauma and scrutiny of their drinking habits — even when they weren’t behind the wheel.

Plaintiffs’ attorneys claim the tactics are designed to undermine their clients’ credibility and make pursuing legal action against the multibillion-dollar company so emotionally and financially exhausting that some may abandon their claims altogether.

The allegations compound revelations in an August New York Times investigation into Uber’s treatment of sexual assault survivors, with attorneys telling The Post that similar tactics are employed even in lawsuits that have nothing to do with sexual violence.

Uber defended its litigation practices.

“We take any claims about personal injury, wrongful death, or sexual assault very seriously,” Katie Waitzman, Uber’s chief deputy general counsel, told The Post. “At the same time, we have a responsibility to defend our company through a legal process that fairly looks at the claims and evidence on both sides.”

Luna Moore, who was awarded $300,000 in a civil arbitration earlier this year, and Normandin-Parker’s parents, who received $40 million, said that no amount of money could undo the emotional toll of the legal battle.

Moore, who says she’s been in regular therapy for PTSD since the fatal ride, still has nightmares about what she might have done to save her friend, part of which was amplified during a roughly nine-hour deposition in which Uber’s attorneys subjected her to a grueling examination of her own life.

“They spent an obscene amount of time asking me what Emily and I were wearing that night,” she recalled.

She said attorneys even attempted to challenge her recollection of the fatal ride based on her inability to remember the brand name of an anti-anxiety medication she had taken as a child.

They then, she recalled, made her disclose details of being sexually assaulted during her adolescence.

“I was forced to share with Uber’s legal team the details and causes of every depressive episode I have ever had, one of which was caused by being raped at the age of 16,” she said.

Perhaps most devastating, Moore recalled being asked what she could have done differently to prevent Emily’s death.

“They spent three years trying to convince me that Emily died because I drank too much.

“Of course the questioning made those feelings worse, on some level,” Moore said of her survivor’s guilt.

“The reason that they ask those things is that they want to break your spirit so that you give up and stop fighting against them.”

Uber expressed its sympathies to Normandin-Parker’s family but said it believes the arbitrator was wrong to hold the company legally responsible for her death.

The invasive questioning extends to routine car accidents, according to California attorney Brooke Soliz Bremmer, who has litigated against Uber in dozens of injury-related cases.

She said passengers have faced questions she believes have little bearing on their injuries — even in crashes involving other drivers.

“My client was not driving the car, and they’re asking whether or not my client had anything to drink,” she told The Post.

Bremmer, who has also represented sexual assault survivors, believes the tactics are intended to put prospective plaintiffs on notice that their entire personal histories could be scrutinized if they take legal action.

“Uber is trying to essentially put women and men, but mostly women, on trial in their deposition room,” she said.

“If you’re demanding a woman’s therapy records all the way back to childhood, that isn’t discovery. It’s absolute intimidation.”

Attorney Alex Boris, who has also represented clients in Uber injury cases, described similarly sweeping demands for psychiatric records and medication histories, even when passengers weren’t making separate claims for psychological injuries.

“They always subpoena basically everything under the sun,” he said.

Boris claimed Uber’s requests for medical records frequently lack time limits, forcing plaintiffs’ attorneys to fight the demands. He also accused the company of prolonging arbitration proceedings, adding time and expense to cases brought by injured passengers.

Uber said examining medical histories is standard practice and helps determine which injuries were actually caused by the incident.

“When Uber is asked to compensate someone for an injury or loss, we are entitled to examine evidence about what caused it and the damages attributable to it,” Waitzman said.

For Moore, despite the emotional toll, she said she never considered abandoning the legal battle.

“Every time Uber’s legal team asked me an inane question, I didn’t feel the urge to back down — I felt the desire to fight back harder,” she said.

Even after the $40 million arbitration award was handed down, Emily’s parents said Uber sought to keep the outcome under wraps. Her father, Ken Parker, told “Good Morning America” in September that Uber wanted the award to remain confidential and proposed a non-disparagement agreement carrying a $10 million penalty for speaking negatively about the company.

Emily’s parents rejected the agreement.

Uber acknowledged that confidentiality was discussed but said it was ultimately not pursued.

In civil litigation, defendants have a legitimate right to investigate whether prior injuries, medical conditions, or traumatic experiences contributed to the harm for which a plaintiff seeks compensation.

But legal experts say the process can morph into a “fishing expedition” when requests become excessively sweeping or have little apparent connection to the claims.

The responsibility for fighting those demands often falls on the very people seeking compensation.

“It seems like a strategic way to impose cost, to impose burden, to take advantage of the fact that a lot of these victims are not going to know what’s permissible discovery and what’s not,” Maria Glover, a Georgetown University law professor who studies complex litigation, told The Post.

Plaintiffs may face additional legal expenses and delays fighting demands for deeply personal records — all while recovering from the very incidents that prompted their lawsuits.

“Discovery is supposed to be broad, but not exceptionally broad,” Glover said.

Nowhere have Uber’s discovery tactics attracted more scrutiny than in its sprawling sexual assault litigation.

“Uber uses discovery to dig into the most painful moments of a survivor’s life,” Sarah London, co-lead counsel in the federal Uber sexual assault multidistrict litigation, told The Post.

“It has sought years of medical records, therapy notes and psychiatric records looking for prior assaults, childhood abuse and mental health history, and it has deposed survivors’ parents, spouses, exes, former work colleagues, and therapists.”

“This is a company that tells its own drivers sexual violence is never the survivor’s fault, then puts survivors’ entire lives on trial,” London said.

Uber said it is focused on defending its safety practices, not scrutinizing survivors’ personal histories, and stressed that it offers support regardless of whether survivors pursue legal action.

“Being survivor-centered and participating in the legal process are not mutually exclusive,” Waitzman said.

The approach, plaintiffs’ attorneys allege, extends into the courtroom.

In April, a federal jury held Uber liable for the assault of passenger Brianna Mensing, and attorneys leading the litigation accused Uber of “dragging her personal history into the courtroom and using it to suggest she was not worthy of belief.”

Some of Uber’s demands have also drawn judicial scrutiny.

In May 2025, U.S. Magistrate Judge Lisa Cisneros found that Uber’s sweeping requests for medical records and documentation of depression, anxiety, PTSD, and even family trauma at any point before or after the alleged assaults were overly broad.

The following month, she also restricted Uber’s requests for years of social-media information.

Uber stressed that courts oversee discovery and pointed to allegedly fabricated ride receipts and other potentially fraudulent claims as reasons for detailed scrutiny.

“Unfortunately, fake claims make it harder for legitimate claimants to have their cases resolved fairly, while undermining confidence in the legal system,” Waitzman said.

Three years after Emily’s death, Moore has given up drinking, moved into her own apartment and is pursuing her ambitions as an author, artist and book editor.

But she said every milestone is tinged with the knowledge that her best friend will never get to experience the same.

“It would be a beautiful feel-good story to say I’m motivated by my own internal strength. I’m not,” Moore said.

“I’m motivated by my love for Emily and my desire to build a life that she will be proud of.”

She is determined to help people impacted by Uber find justice.

That determination kept her fighting during the nearly three-year legal battle.

When she broke down crying during her deposition, Moore recalled, one of Uber’s attorneys asked, “I’m sorry you’re upset. Would you like a break to cry?”

“You’d love it if nobody here had to see me cry,” Moore recalled telling the attorney.

“We’re not taking a break. Next question.”

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Dozens of CBS News staffers have accepted voluntary buyout offers – most drastically hitting the foreign desks in what one staffer called an “extinction level event,” according to a report.

Producers, editors, managers and operational staff are calling it quits in departments across the network, including “60 Minutes,” “CBS Evening News” and the Washington and London bureaus, the Status newsletter reported Friday.

Less than 10% of the CBS News employees who were offered voluntary buyout packages accepted them – a smaller percentage than the average across other Skydance divisions, which were also offered buyouts, a source familiar with the matter told The Post.

At CBS News, it appears no part of the network was hit harder than its London bureau, where more than two dozen staffers opted to accept the buyouts – a painful downsizing for the desk, according to the report.

Wednesday was the deadline for many CBS News employees to accept buyout offers from Skydance, the David Ellison-led giant that recently merged Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery and pledged to cut $6 billion in annual costs within three years.

During the network’s regular editorial meeting on Wednesday morning, CBS News foreign chief Shayndi Raice encouraged those still weighing their options to reach out with any questions – appearing emotional as she spoke, according to Status.

The London departures include a majority of the bureau’s producers; several operational staffers, including head of finance David Magness; and Pete Gow, a veteran “CBS Mornings” producer who has been with the network for more than 20 years, the report said.

Gow’s exit in particular dealt a blow to company morale — he was effectively the bureau’s de facto chief, handling much of the department’s daily logistics after CBS News boss Bari Weiss forced out former bureau chief Claire Day, according to the report.

London staffers decided to take the cash and run for a mix of reasons, potentially because they were offered very generous buyout packages due to the UK’s labor laws, a source told The Post.

Staffers abroad are also growing anxious that once Skydance merges CNN and CBS News, CNN’s more dominant international coverage could squash staffing at their CBS counterparts, the source said.

There’s also widespread disdain in the London bureau for Raice, according to Status, which did not elaborate.

At “60 Minutes” in New York, more than a dozen workers opted to take the buyout offers, though that’s a small fraction of the overall staff and includes no major anchors or reporters, according to the report.

Several staffers at CBS News’ “Evening News” and “CBS Mornings” are also reportedly hitting the doors, as well as some in Washington – though it’s unclear exactly how many in these departments decided to take the offers.

The buyouts come at a turbulent time for the network, after CBS News slashed 6% of its workforce in March.

Weiss then purged top talent at “60 Minutes” – including Scott Pelley, Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega – and brought on new hires, like New York Times columnist Ross Douthat.

Meanwhile, at CNN, some top managers in the New York bureau have accepted buyouts, with one insider describing it as a “brain and production drain,” according to Status.

The offers were first sent out to employees on Oct. 26, less than three weeks after Paramount Skydance closed its $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.

In a memo obtained by The Post, Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz said the exit packages were being offered so workers who don’t see a future at the company can leave.

“As we bring our teams together, we recognize that not everyone will see their future here, and we respect that,” the executives wrote.

Staffers who accept the buyout offers are scheduled to leave Dec. 4, just weeks before Christmas.

It follows Skydance’s $80 billion-plus debt buildup as it formed a mammoth Hollywood conglomerate including CBS, CNN, HBO and Paramount.
news.content: پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. دهها نفر از کارکنان CBS News پیشنهادهای خرید داوطلبانه را پذیرفته اند - طبق گزارشی که یکی از کارکنان آن را "رویداد سطح انقراض" می نامد، به شدت به میزهای خارجی ضربه زده است. خبرنامه Status روز جمعه گزارش داد که تهیه کنندگان، سردبیران، مدیران و کارکنان عملیاتی آن را در بخش های سراسر شبکه، از جمله "60 Minutes"، "CBS Evening News" و دفاتر واشنگتن و لندن ترک می کنند. یک منبع آگاه به The Post گفت که کمتر از 10 درصد از کارمندان CBS News که به آنها بسته های خرید داوطلبانه پیشنهاد شده بود آنها را پذیرفتند - درصدی کمتر از میانگین سایر بخش های Skydance که به آنها نیز پیشنهاد خرید داده شد. در اخبار سی‌بی‌اس، به نظر می‌رسد که هیچ بخشی از شبکه به‌اندازه دفتر لندن آن ضربه سختی ندیده است، جایی که بیش از دوجین کارمند تصمیم گرفتند خریدها را بپذیرند - طبق این گزارش، کاهشی دردناک برای میز. چهارشنبه آخرین مهلتی بود برای بسیاری از کارمندان CBS News برای پذیرش پیشنهادهای خرید Skydance، غول به رهبری دیوید الیسون که اخیراً وارنر Brount را ادغام کرده بود. کشف و متعهد شد که ظرف سه سال 6 میلیارد دلار از هزینه‌های سالانه خود را کاهش دهد. در طول جلسه سرمقاله عادی شبکه در صبح چهارشنبه، شیندی رایس، مدیر خارجی شبکه سی‌بی‌اس، کسانی را که هنوز گزینه‌های خود را بررسی می‌کنند تشویق کرد تا با هر گونه سؤالی صحبت کنند - به گزارش Status، در هنگام صحبت او احساساتی به نظر می‌رسید. خروج از لندن شامل اکثر تهیه‌کنندگان دفتر می‌شود. چندین

Robert Pattinson was watching a gothic horror film when the world learned he’s the new James Bond.

Robert Eggers, Pattinson’s longtime friend and collaborator, told Variety the “Twilight” actor was screening his upcoming movie “Werwulf” when the news broke on Monday.

Ironically, “Werwulf,” which follows a ravenous beast haunting a 14th-century English town, stars Aaron Taylor-Johnson, an early favorite to replace Daniel Craig as the spy agent.

Eggers, who worked with Pattinson on the 2019 horror film “The Lighthouse,” told IGN he was “not surprised” that the British actor was cast as Bond.

“I was just texting him about it this morning,” Eggers also shared.

When asked how Pattinson felt about “Werwulf,” Eggers replied, “Oh, he loved it, of course.”

Pattinson was officially offered the role of Bond on a Sunday phone call, but the news didn’t become public until the next day, according to Variety.

Amazon MGM Studios, which bought the rights to the Bond franchise from the Broccoli family last year, spent between $300,000 and $500,000 on screen tests for the new Bond movie, Variety reported.

Callum Turner, Tom Francis, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor all auditioned for the role, while Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult reportedly emerged as “wildcards” and tested at the last minute.

Director Denis Villeneuve, who worked with Pattinson on the upcoming “Dune: Part 3,” played a pivotal part in the “Batman” star being selected to play 007, two insiders told Variety.

When his casting was announced, Pattinson called the Bond role “an honor of a lifetime.”

“To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement,” he said in a statement. “I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

Christopher Nolan, who directed Pattinson in 2020’s “Tenet” and this year’s “The Odyssey,” joked that Pattinson “is the most cowardly James Bond you’ve ever seen” when he reacted to the casting news earlier this week.

Meanwhile, former Bond Pierce Brosnan congratulated Pattinson on the major career move.

“Dear Robert, Welcome to the world of Bond,” Brosnan wrote on Instagram Wednesday. “You are going to be magnificent.”

The Telegraph reported that filming on Pattinson’s Bond movie could begin as early as next summer.

Pattinson is currently working on “The Batman: Part II,” which temporarily paused filming last month when director Matt Reeves stepped away to deal with a “family matter.”

However, reports state Pattinson may exit the “Batman” franchise before a third film to focus on his new role as Bond.

پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. رابرت پتینسون در حال تماشای یک فیلم ترسناک گوتیک بود که جهان متوجه شد او جیمز باند جدید است. رابرت ایگرز، دوست و همکار قدیمی پتینسون، به Variety گفت که بازیگر "گرگ و میش" در حال نمایش فیلم آینده خود "Werwulf" بود که این خبر روز دوشنبه منتشر شد. از قضا، «ورولف» که به دنبال یک هیولای درنده در یک شهر انگلیسی قرن چهاردهمی است، آرون تیلور جانسون را بازی می‌کند، که یکی از افراد مورد علاقه اولیه برای جایگزینی دنیل کریگ به عنوان مأمور جاسوسی بود. اگرز، که با پتینسون در فیلم ترسناک ۲۰۱۹ «فانوس دریایی» کار می‌کرد، به عنوان یک بازیگر بریتانیایی «فانوس دریایی» کار کرد. باند. ایگرز نیز گفت: «امروز صبح در مورد آن به او پیامک فرستادم. وقتی از پتینسون پرسیده شد که پتینسون در مورد "ورولف" چه احساسی دارد، اگرز پاسخ داد: "اوه، او آن را دوست داشت، البته."
به گفته Variety، استودیوی آمازون MGM که سال گذشته حقوق فرانچایز باند را از خانواده بروکلی خریداری کرد، در یک تماس تلفنی یکشنبه به طور رسمی به پتینسون پیشنهاد شد، اما این خبر تا روز بعد عمومی نشد. کالوم ترنر، تام فرانسیس، جک لودن و جاش اوکانر همگی برای این نقش تست دادند، در حالی که پتینسون و نیکلاس هولت ظاهراً به عنوان «کارت‌های وحشی» ظاهر شدند و در آخرین لحظه آزمایش کردند. کارگردان دنیس ویلنوو، که با پتینسون در فیلم آینده «Dune: Part 3» کار می‌کرد، نقش مهمی را ایفا کرد.

news.originalContent:
The plan would replace the jail complex with four smaller jails and reduce the number of people behind bars.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has unveiled a plan to close the notorious Rikers Island jail complex by 2032, setting out how his administration hopes to shut down a facility long criticised for violence, overcrowding and poor sanitation.

The plan, released on Friday, proposes closing the jail five years after a deadline of August 2027 that was set under then-Mayor Bill de Blasio.

With less than a year to go, the four smaller jails in four New York boroughs that are meant to replace Rikers are still under construction.

The jail complex mostly holds people awaiting trial rather than serving sentences after conviction.

“For decades, New Yorkers have demanded a correctional system that is safe and humane,” said Mamdani in a statement.

“We have a legal and moral obligation to close Rikers,” he said.

The mayor’s strategy involves reducing the number of people held at Rikers from 6,700 to no more than 4,100 by expanding alternatives to detention, restoring online bail payments, investing in programmes that aim to reduce repeat offending, and shortening court delays.

Court delays can leave people “detained for years in what is essentially legal purgatory”, said Mamdani at a news conference on Friday. The city plans to set up a task force to deal with bottlenecks and improve how agencies share evidence.

Under the new timeline, the first replacement jail will open in Brooklyn in 2029, with the rest completed by 2032. The city plans to also make hospital beds available for people in custody who have serious mental health or medical needs.

“Any family member of someone held at Rikers will tell you how isolating that jail is, how it can take hours to visit a loved one,” Mamdani said, adding that the new jails would be closer to courts and public transport, and would help integrate imprisoned New Yorkers back into the city.

Rikers Island, near LaGuardia airport in New York’s East River, opened in 1932 and has long faced criticism over violence, abuse, and unsanitary conditions, with campaigners pushing for its closure for over a decade.

The facility has been tied to cases like that of Kalief Browder, who spent three years there awaiting trial before the charges against him were dismissed. He died by suicide in 2015 aged 22, two years after his release.

City lawmakers voted to close Rikers in 2019, and Mamdani has blamed the city’s inability to meet the 2027 deadline to build the replacement jails on the previous administration.

Once the jail closes, Mamdani said he wants the island to be used for renewable energy and projects to help the city withstand the effects of climate change.

“Our hope is that the new Rikers Island will be unrecognisable,” he said.
news.content: این طرح قرار است مجتمع زندان را با چهار زندان کوچک‌تر جایگزین کند و تعداد افراد زندانی را کاهش دهد. زوهران مامدانی، شهردار شهر نیویورک، طرحی را برای تعطیلی مجتمع زندان بدنام جزیره ریکرز تا سال 2032 رونمایی کرده است و در آن نحوه امیدواری دولت او برای تعطیلی این مرکز که مدت‌هاست به دلیل خشونت، ازدحام بیش از حد و شرایط بهداشتی نامناسب مورد انتقاد قرار گرفته است، تشریح شده است. این طرح که روز جمعه منتشر شد، پیشنهاد می‌کند که این زندان پنج سال پس از مهلت آگوست 2027 که توسط شهردار وقت بیل دِ بلزیو تعیین شده بود، تعطیل شود. در حالی که کمتر از یک سال به این مهلت باقی مانده است، چهار زندان کوچک‌تر در چهار منطقه نیویورک که قرار است جایگزین ریکرز شوند، هنوز در حال ساخت هستند. در مجموعه زندان ریکرز بیشتر افرادی نگهداری می‌شوند که در انتظار محاکمه هستند تا اینکه پس از محکومیت در حال گذراندن محکومیت خود باشند. مامدانی در بیانیه‌ای گفت: «دهه‌هاست که نیویورکی‌ها خواستار یک سیستم اصلاحی ایمن و انسانی هستند.»او گفت: «ما از نظر قانونی و اخلاقی موظفیم رایکرز را تعطیل کنیم.» استراتژی شهردار شامل کاهش تعداد افراد زندانی در رایکرز از 6700 نفر به حداکثر 4100 نفر با گسترش روش‌های جایگزین برای بازداشت، بازگرداندن پرداخت آنلاین وثیقه، سرمایه‌گذاری در برنامه‌هایی که هدفشان کاهش تکرار جرم است و کاهش تأخیرهای دادگاه می‌شود. مامدانی روز جمعه در یک کنفرانس خبری گفت: تأخیرهای دادگاه می‌تواند باعث شود افراد «سال‌ها در چیزی که اساساً برزخ قانونی است، بازداشت شوند». این شهر قصد دارد یک کارگروه برای رسیدگی به مشکلات و بهبود نحوه اشتراک‌گذاری مدارک توسط سازمان‌ها تشکیل دهد. طبق جدول زمانی جدید، اولین زندان جایگزین افتتاح خواهد شد.

news.originalContent:
Anthropic’s listing had been viewed as a potential boost for an industry struggling to regain its footing but that was not the case on Friday.

Anthropic’s much-hyped arrival on Wall Street has fizzled out a day later, as a dramatic unravelling of the artificial intelligence trade showed that even a blockbuster listing could not shake the gloom hanging over the sector.

On Friday, the stock, the biggest public stock offering ever and which surpassed $2 trillion in value at one point, was trading at $87.95, about 9.5 percent down from Thursday’s close, at about 11:30am in New York (16:30 GMT).

Widely seen as a proxy for the AI trade, Anthropic’s listing had been viewed as a potential boost for an industry struggling to regain its footing after a turbulent stretch. But the slump in price within a day of listing – though still higher than its offer price of $83.30 – while losses across other technology heavyweights suggested the IPO had done little to reverse the broader selloff.

“Investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth,” said David Miller, chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds.

Among the Magnificent Seven stocks, Nvidia was down nearly 7 percent, Meta Platforms fell almost 4 percent, while Amazon and Microsoft dropped 2.1 percent and 1.7 percent, respectively.

Chip stocks also slid, with AMD down 11.2 percent, Sandisk down nearly 15 percent and Intel losing 4.3 percent.

More stocks were gaining ground within the S&P 500, but AI stocks with hefty market values have a much bigger impact on the market’s direction. They were responsible for Wall Street’s big gains this year and are now behind the big slide for the market.

AI stocks have been losing ground partly over worries that their big market values and heavy spending are unjustified. Fears of a bubble within the sector have also run up against the recent midterm elections, where there has been a shift in power after the Republican Party, seen as more friendly to the industry, suffered an electoral sweep.

Anthropic’s stock could find support later in the year; London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates index-tracking funds could account for purchases of up to 30 percent of Anthropic’s shares by year-end.

Market debuts for tech companies are often followed by a volatile period. SpaceX, which previously held the title for the biggest IPO, rose nearly 50 percent in its first three days, but fell below its IPO price a month later. On Friday, the stock was down about 7.4 percent.
news.content: فهرست آنتروپیک به عنوان یک تقویت بالقوه برای صنعتی تلقی می شد که در تلاش برای بازیابی جایگاه خود بود، اما روز جمعه اینطور نبود. ورود آنتروپیک به وال استریت که بسیار شایعه شده بود، یک روز بعد از بین رفت، زیرا آشکارسازی چشمگیر تجارت هوش مصنوعی نشان داد که حتی یک فهرست پرفروش نمی تواند تاریکی بخش را متزلزل کند. در روز جمعه، سهام، بزرگترین عرضه عمومی سهام تا کنون و ارزش آن از 2 تریلیون دلار فراتر رفت، در حدود ساعت 11:30 صبح در نیویورک (16:30 به وقت گرینویچ) با قیمت 87.95 دلار معامله شد که حدود 9.5 درصد نسبت به بسته شدن روز پنجشنبه کاهش داشت. پا پس از کشش متلاطم اما کاهش قیمت در عرض یک روز پس از عرضه به بورس – اگرچه هنوز بالاتر از قیمت پیشنهادی آن 83.30 دلار است – در حالی که ضرر در سایر شرکت‌های بزرگ فناوری نشان می‌دهد که IPO کاری برای معکوس کردن فروش گسترده‌تر انجام نداده است. دیوید میلر، مدیر ارشد سرمایه‌گذاری سرمایه‌گذاری Catalyst در این باره گفت: «سرمایه‌گذاران همچنان به هوش مصنوعی اعتقاد دارند، اما در مورد هزینه‌ای که برای این رشد پرداخت خواهند کرد، گزینش‌تر می‌شوند. در میان سهام مجنیفنت سون، انویدیا نزدیک به 7 درصد سقوط کرد، متا پلتفرم تقریباً 4 درصد سقوط کرد، در حالی که آمازون و مایکروسافت به ترتیب 2.1 درصد و 1.7 درصد سقوط کردند. سهام تراشه نیز با کاهش 11.2 درصدی AMD، Sandisk نزدیک به 15 درصد کاهش یافت و اینتل با افت 4.3 درصدی ارزش سهام را از دست داد.

در نخستین محاکمه از این نوع در انگلستان، چهار مرد به اتهام تجاوز و تعرض جنسی به زنی مجرم شناخته شدند که شوهرش ۱۳ سال به او داروی بیهوشی می‌خوراند و بدون اطلاع و رضایتش در معرض تعرض مردان دیگر قرار می‌داد.

جوآن یانگ که از حق قانونی ناشناس ماندن در این نوع پرونده‌ها صرف‌نظر کرده است پس از رای دادگاه گفت: «این آزار هولناک به من ثابت کرد که حتی خانه هم جای امنی نبود. هرگز دوباره احساس امنیت کامل نخواهم کرد. این اتفاقات زندگی من و فرزندانم را ویران کرد.»

او تاکید کرد که برای جلوگیری از تکرار آنچه بر او رفته است، «سکوت جایز نیست.»

او گفت: «کسی که بیش از هر فرد دیگری در دنیا به او اعتماد داشتم، به هولناک‌ترین شکل ممکن به من خیانت کرد.»

فیلیپ یانگ، ۵۰ ساله و شوهر سابق جوآن پیش‌تر به ۵۶ فقره جرم از جمله چشم‌چرانی، خوراندن مواد با قصد ارتکاب جرم، بیهوش کردن، تجاوز جنسی از طریق دخول، تعرض جنسی و انتشار تصاویر و مطالب جنسی اعتراف کرده و مجرم شناخته شده و منتظر تعیین مجازات از سوی دادگاه است. او که پیش‌تر عضو شورای محلی از حزب محافظه‌کار بود در طول ۱۳ سال از طریق وب‌سایت‌ها و اپلیکیشن‌هایی بدون اطلاع همسرش، مردان را به خانه‌شان در سوئیندون واقع در ویلتشر در غرب انگلستان دعوت می‌کرد.

در یکی از این دفعات، جوآن یانگ به هوش آمد و دید به تختش بسته شده است اما او هیچ تصوری از کابوسی که در زمان بیهوشی‌اش در جریان بوده نداشت.

او در سال ۲۰۲۴ به پلیس گفت که وقتی به هوش آمد، چشم‌بند به چشمانش بسته شده بود و دست‌هایش هم مهار شده بود و هنگامی که تلاش ‌کرد چشم‌بندش را بردارد، صدای شوهرش که به گمان او در انتهای تخت ایستاده بود را شنید که به شخص دیگری گفت: «قایم شو». او تازه آن زمان متوجه شد شخص دیگری هم در اتاق خواب آنها حضور دارد. او به کارآگاهان گفت که در ابتدا فکر می‌‌کرده شخص سوم برای تماشای سکس او و شوهرش آنجا حضور داشته است.

پنج‌شنبه ۱۹ نوامبر (۲۸ آبان)، هیئت منصفه دادگاه سلطنتی وینچستر شامل هشت مرد و چهار زن، نورمن مکسونی ۴۸ ساله، ریچارد ویلکینز ۶۲ ساله، کانر سندرسون-دویل ۳۲ ساله و محمد حسن ۳۸ ساله را در چندین فقره جرم جنسی مجرم شناخت. ویلکینز و مکسونی هر یک در یک فقره اتهام تجاوز هم مجرم شناخته شدند.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

این مردان پیشینه‌های گوناگونی دارند. یکی در پروژه‌های هسته‌ای وزارت دفاع بریتانیا کار می‌کرده و دیگری در دهه ۱۹۸۰ راننده کامیون‌های صلیب سرخ به رومانی بوده است.

در جریان محاکمه، دادستانی اعلام کرد این چهار مرد که هیچ‌یک یکدیگر را نمی‌شناختند، پیش از برقراری رابطه جنسی با جوآن یانگ برای کسب رضایت او اقدامی نکرده بودند.

متهمان مدعی شدند که فیلیپ یانگ آن‌ها را فریب داده و آنان تصور می‌کردند جوآن یانگ رضایت دارد و در یک بازی جنسی خود را به خواب زده است.

قاضی دادگاه پیش از اعلام رأی از حاضران خواست آرامش خود را حفظ کنند. هنگام قرائت احکام، جوآن یانگ در جایگاه تماشاگران و در میان اعضای خانواده‌اش نشسته بود و دستانش را روی دهانش گذاشته بود.

قاضی از جوآن یانگ تقدیر کرد و گفت او در طول رسیدگی به این پرونده «شجاعتی شگفت‌انگیز» از خود نشان داده است.

قاضی به چهار مرد گفت هنگام صدور حکم در روزهای ۲۱ و ۲۲ دسامبر باید انتظار مجازات‌های طولانی‌مدت زندان را داشته باشند. سپس نگهبانان آن‌ها از صحن دادگاه خارج کردند. در همین حال اعضای خانواده جوآن یانگ یکدیگر را در آغوش گرفتند.

جوآن یانگ که پارسال از فیلیپ یانگ طلاق گرفت، گفت که این سوءاستفاده‌ها «زندگی‌ای را که می‌شناختم از من گرفته است.» او همچنین گفت که جرایمی که علیه او صورت گرفته «تأثیری ویرانگر» بر زندگی او و فرزندانش گذاشته است.

او پس از اعلام احکام دادگاه در بیرون ساختمان دادگاه گفت: «اگر واقعاً در جلوگیری از سوءاستفاده جدی هستیم، سکوت جایز نیست.»

دختر او، الکس یانگ، در پیامی در شبکه‌های اجتماعی نوشت «کاملاً غیرقابل قبول» است که از سال ۲۰۰۳ تاکنون قانون در انگلستان و ولز تغییری نکرده است. او نوشت: «جامعه پیشرفت کرده، جرم و جنایت هم تغییر کرده است. پس چرا قانون همگام با آن پیشرفت نکرده است؟»

او افزود: «از دولت می‌خواهم این موضوع را در اولویت قرار دهد تا زنان در آینده به‌درستی مورد حمایت قرار گیرند.»

بر اساس «قانون جرایم جنسی ۲۰۰۳» بریتانیا، رضایت فرد برای سکس و تماس جنسی زمانی محرز است که «به انتخاب خود موافقت کند و از آزادی و توانایی لازم برای اتخاذ آن تصمیم برخوردار باشد.»

این پرونده شباهت‌های زیادی با پرونده تجاوزهای مکرر به ژیزل پلیکو در فرانسه دارد؛ پرونده‌ای که کارشناسان آن را نمونه‌ای از سوءاستفاده‌ای «عمیقاً آزارگرانه» توصیف کرده‌اند.

پروفسور میراندا هوروث، مدیر مؤسسه عدالت اجتماعی و جرم در دانشگاه سافک، به بی‌بی‌سی گفت: «اگر فردی با دارو بیهوش شده، در خواب باشد یا هوشیاری نداشته باشد، نمی‌تواند رضایت بدهد.»

این پرونده بازتاب گسترده‌ای در رسانه‌های بریتانیا داشته است. روزنامه دیلی میل از جوآن یانگ با عنوان «شجاع‌ترین زن بریتانیا» یاد کرده است؛ زنی که شوهرش او را بیهوش می‌کرد و مردانی را که خود جذب کرده بود برای تعرض جنسی به خانه شان می‌آورد.

روزنامه دیلی اکسپرس هم در صفحه اول خود او را «شجاع‌تر از آنچه بتوان تصور کرد» توصیف کرده و آنچه بر او گذشته را «غیرقابل بیان» خوانده است.

روزنامه دیلی میرور هم این پرونده را روایت «شجاعت یک زن» دانسته که «با شوهری روبه‌رو شد که به بدترین شکل ممکن به او خیانت کرده بود.»

news.originalContent:
Workers and students take to the streets as protests inspired by demonstrations in France show no sign of abating.

Protesters have rallied across 25 European countries amid a wave of public discontent over issues ranging from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people.

Inspired by demonstrations that have shaken France in recent months, thousands took to the streets in countries including the United Kingdom, Austria, Germany, Spain, Italy, Sweden and Croatia on Friday.

Tens of thousands of workers and students protested in more than 100 Italian cities to demand higher wages ⁠⁠and greater investment in public services.

The rallies coincided with a general strike by Italy’s largest trade union, CGIL, that involved workers in ‌‌both the private and public sectors, including schools and healthcare.

“Across Europe and among ordinary people, the demand for change is growing,” CGIL leader Maurizio Landini said at a rally in Rome.

Demonstrators in Rome threw objects at the Ministry of Education, while in Bologna some protesters clashed with police, news agency ANSA reported. In Milan, demonstrators set fire to a cardboard tanker as well as cardboard figures depicting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and United States President Donald Trump.

The Italian rallies ⁠⁠followed a nationwide mobilisation on October 17 that descended into rioting and looting and prompted the right-wing government of Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni to approve sweeping security measures and deploy the army alongside police in subsequent demonstrations.

Student groups have since continued protests and occupations at schools and universities, with opposition to higher military spending also emerging as a rallying cry.

Opposition leaders joining demonstrations on Friday criticised Meloni’s government and its budget policies amid rising living costs. Elly Schlein, leader of the centre-left Democratic Party, said the 2027 Budget Law “does not have a vision for the future of the country” as it does not help industries but slashes funding for public healthcare and education.

Meanwhile, in Germany, campaign group “Gen Z regelt” (German for “Gen Z sorts it”) said it ⁠⁠was organising protests in 73 cities and towns.

In Berlin, roughly 4,000 people attended a protest in the city’s ⁠⁠Alexanderplatz square.

The Cologne protest drew fewer than the 5,000 people expected, though ⁠⁠demonstrators still numbered in the thousands, police said.

Protesters gathered to call for greater education funding and to oppose a possible return to compulsory military service.

In Austria, several hundred people gathered outside the University of Vienna for a youth-led protest calling for more spending on education and less on weapons. Police dispersed the event after reported disturbances, saying officers used pepper spray and made several arrests.

In Croatia, students boycotted classes and staged protests in about a dozen cities, demanding greater investment in education, housing and public services rather than military spending.

Demonstrations across Europe were inspired by much larger protests in France that began in September and descended into violent confrontations with the police and looting.

On Tuesday, France’s Interior Ministry said a total of 146,000 people took part in protests across the country, with 28,000 in Paris alone. The CGT trade union put the nationwide total at just over 500,000 demonstrators.

The prices paid for everyday items such as food, energy, transport and bills have risen by between 59 and 78 percent since 2000 in France, Italy, Spain and Portugal, according to Eurostat – the European Union’s statistics agency.

Once inflation is taken into account, the average full-time wage in Italy fell by almost 5 percent between 2000 and 2025. Over the same period, real wages rose by 7 percent in Spain, 11 percent in France and 20 percent in Portugal, according to OECD wage data adjusted with Eurostat’s price index.
news.content: کارگران و دانشجویان در حالی که اعتراضات الهام گرفته از تظاهرات در فرانسه هیچ نشانه ای از کاهش نشان نمی دهد به خیابان ها می آیند. معترضان در 25 کشور اروپایی در بحبوحه موجی از نارضایتی عمومی در مورد مسائلی از هزینه های بالای زندگی گرفته تا هزینه های نظامی و بحران آب و هوا تظاهرات کرده اند و فشار بر رهبران سیاسی را که آنها آنها را به نادیده گرفتن نگرانی های جوانان متهم می کنند، تشدید کرده است. با الهام از تظاهراتی که در ماه های اخیر فرانسه را تکان داده است، هزاران نفر در کشورهایی از جمله بریتانیا، اتریش، آلمان، اسپانیا، ایتالیا، سوئد و کرواسی روز جمعه به خیابان ها آمدند. ده ها هزار کارگر و دانشجو در بیش از 100 شهر ایتالیا تظاهرات کردند و خواستار افزایش دستمزدها و سرمایه گذاری بیشتر در خدمات عمومی شدند. این تظاهرات با اعتصاب عمومی بزرگترین اتحادیه کارگری ایتالیا، CGIL، که کارگران بخش خصوصی و دولتی، از جمله مدارس و مراقبت‌های بهداشتی را درگیر کرد، مصادف شد. مائوریتزیو لندینی، رهبر CGIL در تجمعی در رم گفت: «در سراسر اروپا و در میان مردم عادی، تقاضا برای تغییر در حال افزایش است. خبرگزاری آنسا گزارش داد که تظاهرکنندگان در رم اشیایی را به سمت وزارت آموزش پرتاب کردند، در حالی که در بولونیا برخی از معترضان با پلیس درگیر شدند. در میلان، تظاهرکنندگان یک تانکر مقوایی و همچنین مجسمه های مقوایی را که بنیامین نتانیاهو، نخست وزیر اسرائیل و دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور ایالات متحده را نشان می داد، به آتش کشیدند. تظاهرات ایتالیایی به دنبال بسیج سراسری در 17 اکتبر بود که به شورش و غارت و روابط عمومی منجر شد.

news.originalContent:
In a new letter, Congressman Jamie Raskin says officials in the US government are ignoring federal recordkeeping laws.

A top Democrat, who will wield significant investigative powers in the United States Congress starting in January, has warned US law enforcement agencies to preserve records, including encrypted communications on digital messaging apps.

In letters sent on Thursday to the US Department of Justice and Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Congressman Jamie Raskin of Maryland, the next likely chairman of the US House Judiciary Committee, wrote to the cabinet-level agencies to remind their employees of a legal obligation to “safeguard” records against destruction.

Letters were also sent to the heads of three subagencies, including the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Bureau of Prisons (BOP).

Raskin disclosed he has obtained evidence that government officials in the Trump administration have been using non-government apps, like Signal, to send disappearing messages.

The Maryland Democrat, who is currently the Judiciary Committee’s ranking member, appended a screenshot of a Signal exchange between FBI General Counsel Samuel Ramer and Drew Lynch, an associate of President Donald Trump’s eldest son, Donald Trump Jr, showing a conversation where messages were set to automatically delete after one week.

“The FBI’s top lawyer should be ensuring that all 35,000 FBI employees are preserving government and law enforcement records”, Raskin wrote to US Attorney General Todd Blanche.

“Instead, he has conducted official business on a platform specifically configured to erase communications.”

The incident, Raskin wrote, is “just one of many” that have been reported to the Judiciary Committee, raising concern among Democrats that the Trump administration could be ignoring federal recordkeeping laws by destroying documents before likely congressional investigations.

“There is significant evidence that Trump Administration officials have engaged in the widespread destruction, mutilation, and concealment of government records”, Raskin wrote. “This attempt to evade transparency extends to the highest levels of federal agencies, including top-ranking law enforcement officials”.

Raskin instructed the federal officials to take “immediate action to recover these records” from data backups or “associated metadata,” asking them to comply by December 3.

The Trump administration has signalled it intends to fight any probes by US Democrats, who won control of both chambers of the US Congress earlier this month in the country’s midterm elections.

According to a letter viewed by Al Jazeera, the White House’s top lawyer, Will Scharf, wrote to US House Democrats on Wednesday, pushing back against demands from the incoming Democratic majorities, such as Raskin’s, because the new Congress has not yet been sworn in.

“Your demands do not reflect a request of the House, Senate, or a committee to which that body’s oversight authority has been delegated,” Scharf wrote. “As a result, Ranking Member requests in the 119th Congress do not trigger any obligation to ‘accommodate[e] … the needs of the conflicting branches'”.

In response to Raskin’s letter, a White House official told Al Jazeera the administration complies “with all federal record retention laws and regulations”.

The DOJ echoed the White House’s response, saying it “follows all legal requirements for the management of federal records involving its official functions and decisions.”

“The men and women of the DOJ who work tirelessly to arrest and prosecute criminals will not be intimidated by a congressman who once called 2020 riots ‘magnificent’ and ‘nonviolent'”, the agency said about Raskin.

Al Jazeera also reached out to DHS, FBI, ICE and BOP for comment but has not yet heard back.
news.content: جیمی راسکین، نماینده کنگره در نامه‌ای جدید می‌گوید مقامات دولت ایالات متحده قوانین فدرال نگهداری سوابق را نادیده می‌گیرند. یکی از دموکرات‌های ارشد که از ژانویه از اختیارات تحقیقاتی قابل‌توجهی در کنگره ایالات متحده برخوردار خواهد بود، به سازمان‌های مجری قانون ایالات متحده هشدار داده است که سوابق، از جمله ارتباطات رمزگذاری شده در برنامه‌های پیام‌رسان دیجیتال را حفظ کنند. در نامه‌هایی که روز پنج‌شنبه به وزارت دادگستری و وزارت امنیت داخلی ایالات متحده فرستاده شد، جیمی راسکین، نماینده کنگره از مریلند، رئیس احتمالی بعدی کمیته قضایی مجلس نمایندگان آمریکا، به آژانس‌های سطح کابینه نامه نوشت تا به کارکنان خود تعهد قانونی برای «حفظ» سوابق در برابر تخریب را یادآوری کنند. همچنین نامه‌هایی به روسای سه سازمان فرعی، از جمله اداره تحقیقات فدرال (FBI)، اداره مهاجرت و گمرک (ICE) و اداره زندان‌ها (BOP) ارسال شد. راسکین فاش کرد که به شواهدی دست یافته است که نشان می‌دهد مقامات دولتی در دولت ترامپ از برنامه‌های غیردولتی مانند سیگنال برای ارسال پیام‌های ناپدید شده استفاده می‌کنند. دموکرات مریلند که در حال حاضر عضو رده بندی کمیته قضایی است، تصویری از تبادل سیگنال بین مشاور کل اف بی آی ساموئل رامر و درو لینچ، یکی از همکاران پسر ارشد رئیس جمهور دونالد ترامپ، دونالد ترامپ جونیور، ضمیمه کرد و مکالمه ای را نشان داد که در آن پیام ها قرار بود به طور خودکار پس از یک هفته حذف شوند. کارمندان دولت و قانون را حفظ می کنند

news.originalContent:
Daniel Thomas livestreamed himself slashing a dinghy used to bring migrants from France to the UK.

A British far-right anti-immigration activist has been jailed for 15 months for criminal damage for slashing a small boat which had brought migrants from France to the United Kingdom.

Daniel Thomas, also known as “Danny Tommo”, is the founder of the British anti-migrant Patriot Platform group, which mobilised hundreds of protesters earlier this year. He pleaded guilty to criminal damage earlier this month, after slashing the inflatable vessel while a French emergency responder was on board.

Sentencing Thomas on Friday, judge James Newton-Price said the offence “amounted to flagrant interference and a deliberate disruption” of French and British authorities’ important activities in the English Channel.

“They do necessary, highly sensitive and difficult jobs, and which should not be disrupted by a publicity-seeker slashing with a knife a boat they were attempting to recover,” he added.

Thomas livestreamed himself on September 22 as he followed a small boat ⁠⁠carrying migrants across the Channel, who were transferred ⁠⁠onto another vessel and taken ashore.

The 37-year-old later approached the dinghy and slashed it with a knife, soon after a French rescue worker had stepped on board. British police arrested him shortly after the incident.

Prosecutor Joel Smith told Portsmouth Crown Court that Thomas had shouted “get off the boat, you’ve got time to get off the ⁠⁠boat … take them back, no more ⁠⁠of these”.

Thomas appeared in court via videolink from prison, with his head bowed and rarely looked up as footage of ‌‌the incident was played.

Judge Newton-Price accepted that “there was no immediate danger to the rescue worker”, but said Thomas’s actions were a deliberate ‌‌attempt ‌‌to disrupt rescue efforts.

The far-right activist had built a large online following and organised gatherings of protesters on the UK’s southern coast in response to the arrivals of small boats.

A government minister described the demonstrations as “thuggish”.

The court heard that Thomas had five previous convictions, including in 2016 for kidnapping.

Separately, he is set to stand trial in London next June accused of multiple offences, including entering a restricted zone at a migrant processing centre in Dover in March.

UK government data shows the number of people arriving in small boats to British shores has fallen, though the crossings remain a prominent political issue which has dogged successive governments. Right-wing opposition parties and anti-immigration activists have called for more action.
news.content: دنیل توماس در جریان زنده پخش مستقیم قایق خود را که برای آوردن مهاجران از فرانسه به بریتانیا استفاده می شد، برید. یک فعال راست افراطی بریتانیایی ضد مهاجرت به دلیل آسیب جنایتکارانه به خاطر بریدن قایق کوچکی که مهاجران را از فرانسه به بریتانیا آورده بود، به 15 ماه زندان محکوم شد. معترضان اوایل امسال او در اوایل این ماه پس از بریدن کشتی بادی در حالی که یک امدادگر اضطراری فرانسوی در کشتی بود، به خسارت جنایی اعتراف کرد. قاضی جیمز نیوتن پرایس در محکومیت توماس در روز جمعه گفت که این جرم "مداخله آشکار و اختلال عمدی" در فعالیت های مهم مقامات فرانسوی و بریتانیایی در کانال انگلیسی است. او افزود: «آنها کارهای ضروری، بسیار حساس و دشوار را انجام می‌دهند و نباید توسط یک جوینده تبلیغاتی که با چاقو قایق‌ای را که می‌خواستند آن را بازیابی کنند، می‌تراشد، مختل شود. این مرد 37 ساله بعداً به قایق نزدیک شد و بلافاصله پس از ورود یک امدادگر فرانسوی به قایق، آن را با چاقو برید. پلیس بریتانیا او را اندکی پس از این حادثه دستگیر کرد. دادستان جوئل اسمیت به دادگاه ولیعهد پورتسموث گفت که توماس فریاد زده بود "از قایق پیاده شو، وقت داری که از قایق پیاده شوی...

اندی برنام، نخست‌وزیر بریتانیا و رهبران اتحادیه اروپا، پس از نشستی در بروکسل، از توافقی برای همکاری‌های نزدیک‌تر خبر دادند.

آقای برنام این توافق را «برد-برد» خواند و اظهار امیدواری کرد که این توافق هزینه زندگی را برای مصرف‌کنندگان کاهش دهد و از پیچیدگی‌های اداری برای کسب‌وکارها بکاهد.

او گفت که افکار عمومی در بریتانیا، ۱۰ سال پس از همه‌پرسی برای خروج از اتحادیه اروپا، امروز خواهان نزدیکتر شدن روابط با این اتحادیه است.

اورزولا فون درلاین، رئیس کمیسیون اروپا، این توافق را «نقطه عطفی» در روابط بین بریتانیا و اتحادیه اروپا دانست و به توافقی دوجانبه برای تردد آزاد جوانان اشاره کرد.

به گفته مقام‌های حاضر در این نشست، همچنین توافق‌هایی در زمینه مقررات تجارت مواد غذایی و سهمیه‌ انتشار گازهای آلاینده حاصل شده است.

با این حال، اتحادیه اروپا می‌گوید که تمامی این موارد مشروط به دستیابی به توافقی در خصوص شهریه دانشگاه‌ها برای دانشجویان اروپایی در بریتانیا طی شش ماه آینده است.

آقای برنام گفت: «امروز روز خوبی برای بریتانیا و روز خوبی برای اروپا است. مردم سراسر اروپا و بریتانیا از این توافق بهره‌های واقعی خواهند برد.»

او افزود که این توافق «امیدی برای کاهش هزینه‌های خرید مایحتاج هفتگی است» و باعث «کاهش تشریفات اداری دست‌ و پاگیر» برای کسب‌وکارها خواهد شد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

آقای برنام همچنین گفت کسانی که «نگران مهاجران غیرقانونی هستند بی‌تردید از شنیدن خبر مشارکت بریتانیا در "طرح اقدام کانال مانش" خرسند خواهند شد.»

او همچنین گفت: «امروز روز بسیار خوبی برای جوانان بریتانیاست؛ بالاخره کورسوی امیدی در افق پدیدار شده است.»

نخست‌وزیر بریتانیا می‌گوید توافق او با اتحادیه اروپا، تا نیم درصد به تولید ناخالص داخلی کشورش خواهد افزود و آن را «بزرگ‌ترین اقدام واحد برای رشد در دولت فعلی» خواند.

آقای برنام در بیانیه‌ای پیش از اجلاس امروز گفت که این توافق «هزینه‌ها را کاهش خواهد داد، قیمت‌ها را در سوپرمارکت‌ها پایین نگه خواهد داشت و فرصت‌هایی را برای جوانان ایجاد خواهد کرد.»

در این بیانیه‌‌ که دفتر نخست‌وزیری بریتانیا آن را منتشر کرده، آمده که دولت رویکردی «مشارکتی و عمل‌گرایانه» را برای مذاکرات با اتحادیه اروپا در پیش گرفته است؛ «آزمون این اجلاس ساده است: آیا زندگی مردم بریتانیا را بهتر می‌کند؟»

آقای برنام، از جمله اولویت‌های طرح خود به این موارد اشاره کرد:

آقای برنام افزود: «بریتانیا و اروپا ارزش‌ها، منافع و همسایگی جهانی مشترکی دارند. با افزایش خطرهای جهانی، ما با هم قوی‌تر هستیم. همکاری نزدیک‌تر با اروپا برای طبقه کارگر، برای بریتانیا و برای اروپا خوب است.»

بر اساس اطلاعات دریافتی بی‌بی‌سی، یکی از توافق‌هایی که قرار است امروز نهایی شود، طرح جدیدی برای «پذیرش جوانان» است که به موجب آن، سالانه تا ۱۰۰ هزار جوان از کشورهای اتحادیه اروپا می‌توانند به بریتانیا سفر و کار کنند و به تحصیل بپردازند.

در چارچوب همین طرح، به همین تعداد از جوانان بریتانیایی نیز اجازه داده خواهد شد که به کشورهای اروپایی بروند.

بریتانیا در حال حاضر طرح‌های مشابهی با ۱۳ کشور غیرعضو اتحادیه اروپا، از جمله استرالیا، هند و کانادا، دارد.

جاناتان رینولدز، وزیر تجارت بریتانیا، می‌گوید عوامل بسیاری بر قیمت مواد غذایی تأثیرگذارند.

به گفته آقای رینولدز هزینه‌ای که برداشته می‌شود در «حذف بوروکراسی، تردد راحت‌تر در مرزها و حذف بازرسی‌های فیزیکی و الکترونیکی» خواهد بود.

او گفت پس از خروج بریتانیا از اتحادیه اروپا، یک‌هفتم کسب‌وکارها در بریتانیا صادرات خود را به‌کلی متوقف کردند و صنایع غذایی و کشاورزی از آن زمان، متحمل «فشارهای سنگین» شده‌اند.

وزیر تجارت گفت که نمی‌تواند با قاطعیت بگوید که قیمت مواد غذایی ارزان‌تر خواهد شد، چرا که «عوامل دیگری نیز دخیل هستند.»

او به مواردی همچون قیمت انرژی، روند تجارت جهانی و جنگ ایران بنوان برخی از این عوامل اشاره کرد.

کمی بدناک، رهبر حزب محافظه‌کار، به بی‌بی‌سی گفت که خواهان تسهیل تجارت با اتحادیه اروپا است، اما نه «به هر قیمتی».

او همچنین گفت که توافق‌ جدید ممکن است شرکت‌های بریتانیایی را ملزم به پیروی از قوانین اتحادیه اروپا کند حتی اگر با این اتحادیه دادوستد نداشته باشند.

خانم بدناک افزود که قرار گرفتن در وضعیتی که «بدترین ویژگی‌های هر دو حالت» را داشته باشد، یعنی خروج از اتحادیه اروپا و در عین حال تن دادن به قوانین آن «نامطلوب» است.

حزب لیبرال دموکرات نیز در بیانیه‌ای گفت که نزدیک‌تر شدن با اروپا، بریتانیا را از نظر اقتصادی و امنیتی، قوی‌تر و امن‌تر می‌کند اما تاکید کرد که «نخست‌وزیر باید به وعده‌های خود عمل کند.»

نایجل فاراژ، رهبر حزب «اصلاح» بریتانیا به طرح پیشنهادی «پذیرش جوانان» حمله کرد.

آقای فاراژ به بی‌بی‌سی گفت: «ما در حال گشودن مسیر سیاست "درهای باز" برای مهاجرت از سایر نقاط اروپا هستیم.»

او این توافق را «اشتباهی بسیار پرهزینه و گران‌» خواند و گفت که نخست‌وزیر بریتانیا هیچ‌گونه «مشروعیتی» برای انجام چنین توافقی ندارد.

آقای فاراژ که از پیشگامان طرح خروج بریتانیا از اتحادیه اروپا بود همچنین گفت که به باور او، پیوستن به بازار انرژی اروپا، باعث افزایش هزینه‌های انرژی مصرف‌کنندگان خواهد شد.

اندی برنام، نخست‌وزیر بریتانیا و رهبران اتحادیه اروپا، پس از نشستی در بروکسل، از توافقی برای همکاری‌های نزدیک‌تر خبر دادند.

او گفت که افکار عمومی در بریتانیا، ۱۰ سال پس از همه‌پرسی برای خروج از اتحادیه اروپا، امروز خواهان نزدیکتر شدن روابط با این اتحادیه است.

اورزولا فون درلاین، رئیس کمیسیون اروپا، این توافق را «نقطه عطفی» در روابط بین بریتانیا و اتحادیه اروپا دانست و به توافقی دوجانبه برای تردد آزاد جوانان اشاره کرد.
